docs.title: AI Codebase Knowledge Builder
docs.text: Ever stared at a new codebase written by others feeling completely lost? This project analyzes GitHub repositories and creates beginner-friendly tutorials explaining exactly how the code works - all powered by AI! Our intelligent system automatically breaks down complex codebases into digestible explanations that even beginners can understand.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Clone this repository 

    git clone https://github.com/ardennguyen/Codebase-Knowledge-Builder

  2. Install dependencies (we highly recommend using a virtual environment of your choice like venv, conda, uv, or pyenv to avoid polluting your global system): 

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  3. Set up LLM in utils/call_llm.py by providing credentials via a .env file. You can use native Gemini by setting GEMINI_API_KEY. For OpenRouter, set LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER and OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

  4. Generate a complete codebase tutorial by running the main script: 

    # Analyze a GitHub repository
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --include "*.py" "*.js" --exclude "tests/*" --max-size 50000

# Or, analyze a local directory
python main.py --dir /path/to/your/codebase --include "*.py" --exclude "*test*"

# Or, generate a tutorial in Vietnamese
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --language "Vietnamese"

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text:
• --repo or --dir - Specify either a GitHub repo URL or a local directory path (required, mutually exclusive)
  • -n, --name - Project name (optional, derived from URL/directory if omitted)
  • -t, --token - GitHub token (or set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable)
  • -o, --output - Output directory (default: ./output)
  • -i, --include - Files to include (e.g., *.py *.js). Defaults to * (all files).
  • -e, --exclude - Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.
  • -s, --max-size - Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200KB)
  • --language - Language for the generated tutorial (default: "english")
  • --max-abstractions - Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10)
  • --no-cache - Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled)
  • --thinking-level - Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.
  • --max-tokens - Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically from the model).
  • --mode - Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial)
  • --advanced - Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced
  • --mkdocs - Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet)
  • --incremental - Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference)
  • --batch - Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).
  • --force-batch - Force the pipeline to use map-reduce mode regardless of context limits.
  • --debug - Enable verbose debug output.
  • --cleanup - Clean up logs and cache JSON at the end of the script (default: No).

The application will crawl the repository, analyze the codebase structure, generate tutorial content in the specified language, and save the output in the specified directory (default: ./output). This includes individual chapter files, an index.md, and a compiled full_content.md containing the complete tutorial with a Table of Contents.

Built using Pocket Flow, a 100-line LLM framework.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
Notes for AI: Keep it simple and clear. If the requirements are abstract, write concrete user stories

User Story: As a developer onboarding to a new codebase, I want a tutorial automatically generated from its GitHub repository or local directory, optionally in a specific language. The system supports four documentation styles: a tutorial mode that explains core abstractions with beginner-friendly language, analogies, and code walkthroughs; an advanced mode that produces architecture deep-dives aimed at senior developers or PMs joining a project mid-way, covering design patterns, key dependencies, and practical onboarding notes; an api-reference mode that generates exhaustive, formal API documentation for every code module (1:1 file-to-chapter mapping); and an sdk mode that produces SDK-style integration guides. The system must also gracefully handle codebases of any size by dynamically switching to a Map-Reduce approach when context limits are reached.

Input: - A publicly accessible GitHub repository URL or a local directory path. - A project name (optional, will be derived from the URL/directory if not provided). - Desired language for the tutorial (optional, defaults to English). - Advanced configurations: documentation style (--mode), token scaling (--max-tokens, --batch, --force-batch), prompting (--thinking-level, --max-abstractions), caching (--no-cache), output format (--mkdocs, --incremental), debugging (--debug), and execution cleanup (--cleanup).

Output: - A directory named after the project containing: - An index.md file with: - A high-level project summary (potentially translated). - A Mermaid flowchart diagram visualizing relationships between abstractions (using potentially translated names/labels). - An ordered list of links to chapter files (using potentially translated names). - A link to full_content.md at the bottom. - Individual Markdown files for each chapter (01_chapter_one.md, 02_chapter_two.md, etc.) detailing core abstractions in a logical order (potentially translated content). - A full_content.md (inside the project subdirectory) containing all merged chapters and a Table of Contents. - When --mkdocs is used: YAML frontmatter is injected into every chapter, filenames mirror source directory structure instead of numbered prefixes, and a nav_snippet.yml navigation file is generated for MkDocs integration. - When --incremental is used (api-reference mode only): a .doc_cache_manifest.json tracks MD5 hashes of source files to skip regeneration of unchanged modules across runs.

docs.title: 2. Flow Design
docs.text: Notes for AI: 1. Consider the design patterns of agent, map-reduce, rag, and workflow. Apply them if they fit. 2. Present a concise, high-level description of the workflow.

docs.title: Applicable Design Pattern:
docs.text:
This project primarily uses a Workflow pattern with dynamic branching into a Map-Reduce pattern. The chapter writing step also utilizes a BatchNode.

  1. Workflow & Routing: The overall process fetches code, estimates token payloads, and routes based on context limits. If the codebase fits the LLM window, it goes directly to abstraction identification.
  2. Map-Reduce: If the codebase exceeds context limits (or if forced), the codebase is grouped into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (each batch stays under the effective token limit and never mixes files from different directories). A MapAbstractions BatchNode processes each batch individually, and a ReduceAbstractions Node merges them into a global list.
  3. Batch Processing: The WriteChapters node processes each identified abstraction independently (map) before final tutorial compilation.

docs.title: Flow high-level Design:
docs.text:
1. FetchRepo: Crawls the specified repository/directory using crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files.
  2. ContextRouter: Analyzes the total token payload of the fetched files using tiktoken. Dynamically calculates prompt overhead (template tokens + directory tree tokens) and computes an effective limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead. If --mode api-reference is used, routes to "deterministic". If the file content tokens exceed this effective limit or if --force-batch is used, it chunks files into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (never mixing files from different directories) and routes to "batch". Also builds a compact directory tree of all files (stored in shared["directory_tree"]) for cross-batch awareness. With --debug, displays detailed per-batch file lists and token breakdowns. Otherwise, it routes to "direct".
  3. Path A: Direct
    • IdentifyAbstractions: Analyzes the entire codebase at once to identify core abstractions.
  4. Path B: Map-Reduce
    • MapAbstractions (BatchNode): Analyzes each localized directory chunk to extract partial abstractions. Each batch receives the full directory tree for cross-batch awareness.
    • ReduceAbstractions: Merges overlapping/partial abstractions into a global list of architecture components.
  5. Path C: Deterministic (api-reference mode)
    • DeterministicFileMapper: Bypasses LLM-based abstraction discovery entirely. Uses a lightweight LLM call to filter out non-code files (configs, UI layouts, static assets), then creates a 1:1 mapping of each code file to a documentation module. Skips AnalyzeRelationships and OrderChapters, routing directly to WriteChapters.
  6. AnalyzeRelationships (Paths A & B only): Takes the unified abstractions list (from either path) and generates a high-level project summary and relationships diagram. Uses token-budget-aware file inclusion: the budget is split evenly across abstractions, with unused budget redistributed in a second pass, maximizing code context without exceeding the context window.
  7. OrderChapters (Paths A & B only): Determines the most logical sequence to present the abstractions.
  8. WriteChapters (BatchNode): Iterates through the ordered abstractions and writes detailed Markdown chapters using context-aware code inclusion.
  9. CombineTutorial: Assembles the final outputs including index.md, individual chapter files, and a compiled full_content.md.
flowchart TD
    A[FetchRepo] --> Router[ContextRouter]

    Router -->|direct| B[IdentifyAbstractions]
    Router -->|batch| M1[MapAbstractions]
    Router -->|deterministic| DFM[DeterministicFileMapper]
    M1 --> M2[ReduceAbstractions]

    B --> C[AnalyzeRelationships]
    M2 --> C

    C --> D[OrderChapters]
    D --> E[Batch WriteChapters]
    DFM --> E
    E --> F[CombineTutorial]

def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None,
                      max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True) -> dict:
    # Returns: {"files": {relative_path_str: content_str, ...}}

Directory Pruning Algorithm (critical for nested directories like Core.User/.vs/): 

# During os.walk, for each subdirectory d:
excluded_dirs = set()
for d in dirs:
    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)
    # Check .gitignore first
    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
        excluded_dirs.add(d)
        continue
    # Check exclude patterns — strip trailing /* for directory matching
    if exclude_patterns:
        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
            dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                break
# Remove matched dirs to prevent os.walk descent
for d in dirs.copy():
    if d in excluded_dirs:
        dirs.remove(d)

Note: Directory validation: raises ValueError if directory path doesn't exist. Loads .gitignore with utf-8-sig encoding (BOM-safe). All directories and files are sorted() for deterministic traversal order.

Progress Display Format: - Green (\033[92m): [processed] — Successfully read files - Gray (\033[90m): [excluded (.gitignore)] / [excluded (not in include list)] — Skipped by pattern - Red (\033[91m): [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB] — Exceeded max_file_size - Red (\033[91m): [cannot process: not a text file] / [cannot process: {e}] — Binary/encoding errors

Note: After crawling, prints a --- Crawl Summary --- block with total found, processed, excluded, size limited, and non-text counts.

    files = {}
    skipped_files = []

    # --- ANSI colors ---
    C_GREEN  = "\033[92m"
    C_GRAY   = "\033[90m"
    C_RED    = "\033[91m"
    C_RESET  = "\033[0m"

    # --- Counters ---
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_list = []
    skipped_non_text_list = []
    entry_num = 0

    # --- Load .gitignore (BOM-safe) ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
    gitignore_spec = None
    if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
        try:
            with open(gitignore_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
        except Exception:
            pass

    for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
        # --- Directory pruning (same algorithm as crawl_local_files) ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break
            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)
        dirs.sort()  # Deterministic traversal order

        # --- File processing ---
        for filename in sorted(filenames):
            abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
            rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
            entry_num += 1

            if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
            except OSError:
                continue

            if file_size > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                size_kb = file_size / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                with open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files[rel_path] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")

    # --- Crawl Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    print(f"\n--- Crawl Summary ---")
    print(f"  Total found : {total_fetched}")
    print(f"{C_GREEN}  Processed   : {count_processed}{C_RESET}")
    if count_excluded > 0:
        print(f"{C_GRAY}  Excluded    : {count_excluded}{C_RESET}")
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Size limit  : {count_size_limit}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_size_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    if count_non_text > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Non-text    : {count_non_text}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_non_text_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    print(f"---------------------")

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": len(skipped_files),
            "skipped_files": skipped_files,
            "base_path": None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
            "source": "ssh_clone"
        }
    }

Step 4 — Recursive Content Fetching (1 API call per directory): 

def fetch_contents(path):
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
    params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

    # Rate limit handling with header-based wait:
    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and 'rate limit exceeded' in response.text.lower():
        if not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Provide a token.")
        reset_time = int(response.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Reset', 0))
        wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
        time.sleep(wait_time)
        return fetch_contents(path)  # Recursive retry

    contents = response.json()
    if not isinstance(contents, list):
        contents = [contents]

    for item in contents:
        if item["type"] == "file":
            # Check patterns, size, then fetch content
            # Path A: Use download_url directly, check Content-Length header
            # Path B (fallback): If no download_url, GET item["url"],
            #   base64 decode with size estimate: len(content) * 0.75 > max_file_size
        elif item["type"] == "dir":
            # Check gitignore + exclude before recursing
            fetch_contents(item["path"])

Step 5 — Dual Content Fetch Strategy: 

# Path A: download_url available
if "download_url" in item and item["download_url"]:
    file_response = requests.get(item["download_url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get('content-length', 0))
    if content_length > max_file_size:  # Final size check
        continue
    files[rel_path] = file_response.text

# Path B: base64 fallback
else:
    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_data = content_response.json()
    if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size
        continue
    file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode('utf-8')
    files[rel_path] = file_content

No LLM call. Routes to "direct" or "batch". Writes shared["max_tokens"], shared["file_batches"], shared["directory_tree"].

ContextRouter Algorithm: 1. Auto-detect max_tokens from provider if not set; write to shared["max_tokens"] 2. Notes for AI: Each node handles malformed LLM output differently. This table determines whether a node retries (via PocketFlow's retry mechanism) or silently skips bad items.

Node Validation Style Behavior on Invalid Output FetchRepo Strict Raises ValueError if 0 files crawled ContextRouter N/A Internal math, no LLM output to validate IdentifyAbstractions Strict on structure, lenient on indices Raises ValueError if not list, missing keys, or wrong types → triggers retry. Invalid individual indices are silently skipped with a warning. MapAbstractions Lenient Silently skips malformed items (missing keys, wrong types). Does NOT raise ValueError. ReduceAbstractions Lenient Same as MapAbstractions — silently skips invalid items. docs.text:
Notes for AI: Prompt templates are in prompts/tutorial/, prompts/advanced/, prompts/api-reference/, and prompts/sdk/. They contain {placeholder} variables that form a CONTRACT with the node code.

  1. NEVER paraphrase, truncate, or summarize prompt templates — copy them byte-for-byte from the originals
  2. The {variable} placeholders are a CONTRACT — nodes MUST pass exactly matching kwargs to .format()
  3. To verify correctness: grep each template for {word} patterns. Every match must appear as a kwarg in the corresponding node's .format() call
  4. Templates use Python .format() syntax — any literal { or } in template text MUST be escaped as {{ or }}
  5. All 4 directories (tutorial/, advanced/, api-reference/, sdk/) have the SAME 6 template files. The tutorial/ and advanced/ directories share identical placeholder names. The api-reference/ and sdk/ templates may have different placeholder sets (e.g., api-reference/draft_chapters.md omits {tone_note}, {chapter_num}, {instruction_lang_note}, {code_comment_note}, {mermaid_lang_note}).

docs.text:
Notes for AI: This is the EXACT content of flow.py. Reproduce it exactly.

from pocketflow import Flow
from nodes import (
    FetchRepo, ContextRouter, MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions,
    IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters,
    WriteChapters, CombineTutorial, DeterministicFileMapper
)

def create_tutorial_flow():
    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode
    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),

def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

docs.text: File Path: flow.py

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The flow module defines the core directed acyclic graph (DAG) workflow for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder using the pocketflow framework. It configures and links all execution nodes responsible for repository fetching, context routing, abstraction mapping, chapter sequencing, content writing, and tutorial synthesis.

Depending on the context routing strategy selected during execution (direct, batch, or deterministic), the workflow dynamically branches to process codebase contexts of varying sizes before converging to write chapters and assemble the final tutorial.

docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow:

Description: Instantiates and configures the pocketflow.Flow computational graph for the tutorial generation pipeline. It initializes all workflow nodes with operational parameters (such as max_retries=5 and wait=20 seconds for LLM-bound operations) and sets up the node routing topology:

  1. Initialization: Creates instances of FetchRepo, ContextRouter, MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, CombineTutorial, and DeterministicFileMapper.
  2. Repository Fetch & Routing: Connects FetchRepo to ContextRouter.
  3. Branching Paths:
  4. "direct" route: Routes to IdentifyAbstractions for codebases fitting in single-prompt contexts.
  5. "batch" route: Routes to MapAbstractions followed by ReduceAbstractions for larger multi-batch codebases.
  6. "deterministic" route: Routes to DeterministicFileMapper for file-by-file deterministic chapter mappings.
  7. Synthesis & Convergence:
  8. Connects IdentifyAbstractions and ReduceAbstractions into AnalyzeRelationships.
  9. Connects AnalyzeRelationships to OrderChapters, which leads into WriteChapters.
  10. Connects DeterministicFileMapper directly into WriteChapters.
  11. Routes WriteChapters into CombineTutorial for the final markdown aggregation.

Parameters: None

Returns: * Flow: An initialized pocketflow.Flow pipeline with FetchRepo configured as the entry point node (start).

Raises: None directly raised during declaration.*

Example: 

from flow import create_tutorial_flow

# Instantiate the pipeline
tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()

# Execute the flow with shared context dictionary
shared_context = {
    "repo_path": "https://github.com/example/repo",
    "output_dir": "./output"
}
tutorial_flow.run(shared_context)

Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: Executes the primary CLI application logic. It parses arguments, resolves target repository/directory settings, dynamically inspects environment variables for provider configuration, configures logging via utils.call_llm, builds the shared flow context dictionary, runs the workflow DAG generated by flow, and performs cleanup if requested.

docs.title: Core Implementation:

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a tutorial for a GitHub codebase or local directory.")

    # Create mutually exclusive group for source
    source_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    source_group.add_argument("--repo", help="URL of the public GitHub repository.")
    source_group.add_argument("--dir", help="Path to local directory.")

    # ... [Argument parsing configuration] ...

    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Get GitHub token from argument or environment variable if using repo
    github_token = None
    if args.repo:
        github_token = args.token or os.environ.get('GITHUB_TOKEN')
        if not github_token:
            print("Warning: No GitHub token provided. You might hit rate limits for public repositories.")

    # Resolve mode (backward compatibility for --advanced)
    doc_mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and doc_mode != "api-reference":
        print("\n\033[93m[Warning] --incremental caching is only effective in 'api-reference' mode due to stable 1:1 file mapping. Disabling incremental cache for this run.\033[0m\n")
        args.incremental = False

    # Prepare shared store to be passed between nodes
    shared = {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": args.name,
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        "language": args.language,
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        "mode": doc_mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": doc_mode == "advanced",
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        "debug": args.debug,
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None
    }

    # ... [LLM config & context length resolution] ...

    # Create the flow instance
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()

    # Run the flow
    tutorial_flow.run(shared)

    # Cleanup logs and cache if requested
    if args.cleanup:
        # ... [Cleanup implementation] ...

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The nodes.py module defines the execution nodes that form the core transformation pipeline of Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. Built on top of the pocketflow framework (Node and BatchNode abstractions), these classes implement a map-reduce pipeline that ingests source repositories, filters non-code assets, identifies domain abstractions via Large Language Models (LLMs), discovers cross-module relationships, orders chapters logically, and synthesizes structured tutorials or API documentation (including MkDocs outputs).

The lifecycle of each node follows PocketFlow's three-phase execution model: 1. prep(shared): Extracts and formats necessary inputs from the shared state dictionary into immutable argument bundles. 2. exec(prep_res) / exec(item): Performs isolated computation, file parsing, token estimation, and LLM inference. 3. post(shared, prep_res, exec_res): Validates results, transforms data, updates the shared memory dictionary, and returns the next execution action/route.

    end

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data: list, indices: list) -> dict:

Description: Extracts file contents from a master list of (path, content) tuples for a specific subset of numerical indices. Keys in the returned dictionary are formatted as "{index} # {path}" to provide LLM context identifying the file's index and path simultaneously.

Parameters: * files_data (list): List of tuples where each element is (path, content). * indices (list): Collection of integer indices indicating which files to extract.

Returns: * dict: Mapping of formatted index-path strings to file contents.

Raises: * None. Out-of-bounds indices are ignored via boundary checks (0 <= i < len(files_data)).

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = (
                content  # Use index + path as key for context
            )
    return content_map

The function iterates over the requested index list and safely resolves each entry against the files_data collection. By using {i} # {path} as dictionary keys, downstream nodes can construct prompt payloads where the language model retains visibility into both the positional offset and directory path of each relevant file.

docs.title: load_prompt_template()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name: str, advanced_mode: bool = False, mode: str = None) -> str:

Description: Loads a prompt Markdown template from the disk under the prompts/ directory relative to the current file. It resolves the directory by prioritizing explicit mode overrides (mode), falling back to "advanced" if advanced_mode is enabled, or defaulting to "tutorial".

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base name of the template file (without .md). * advanced_mode (bool, optional): Flag indicating whether to use advanced prompts when mode is unspecified. Defaults to False. * mode (str, optional): Specific subfolder name under prompts/ (e.g., "tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Raw template contents read using utf-8-sig encoding.

Raises: * FileNotFoundError: If the constructed template path does not exist on disk. * IOError: If read operations fail.

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                        "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return f.read()

The function resolves relative paths by determining the absolute directory containing nodes.py via __file__. It applies utf-8-sig encoding to handle potential byte order marks (BOM) in custom prompt files gracefully, returning raw template strings ready for .format() interpolation.

docs.title: parse_yaml_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response: str) -> object:

Description: Extracts and parses a YAML block from an LLM response string. It identifies content wrapped in yaml ... code fences and deserializes it into Python native structures using PyYAML's yaml.safe_load.

Parameters: * response (str): Raw LLM textual response expected to contain a fenced YAML block.

Returns: * object: Parsed YAML structure (list, dict, etc.).

Raises: * ValueError: If code fences are missing or if YAML parsing fails.

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}")

This helper handles structured output extraction across all nodes communicating with the LLM. It splits on yaml` and delimiters, trims whitespace, and calls yaml.safe_load. If the LLM generates malformed YAML or fails to include code blocks, the helper raises a ValueError with descriptive debugging context.

docs.title: create_token_counter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_token_counter() -> callable:

Description: Factory function returning a token counting callable. It attempts to load tiktoken with the cl100k_base encoding (used by modern OpenAI and compatible models). If tiktoken fails or is unavailable, it returns a fallback lambda calculating heuristic token length (len(text) // 4).

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * callable: A function accepting text: str and returning token count as int.

Raises: * None. Catches internal exceptions during tokenizer initialization.

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

The token counter enables offline context sizing across routing and prompt generation stages. Disabling special tokens (disallowed_special=()) prevents exceptions when source code contains syntax resembling tokenizer control sequences.

docs.title: resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_max_tokens(shared: dict) -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum token limit for the current execution run. If max_tokens is explicitly set in shared, that value is returned. Otherwise, it inspects environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, GEMINI_MODEL, GEMINI_API_KEY, etc.) and calls get_model_context_length to query provider defaults dynamically.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary.

Returns: * int: Resolved token limit for prompt budgets.

Raises: * None. Falls back through provider-specific environment variables.

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def resolve_max_tokens(shared):
    """Resolve max_tokens from shared store or auto-detect from provider env vars."""
    max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens")
    if max_tokens is not None:
        return max_tokens
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider == "GEMINI" or not provider:
        endpoint = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com"
        model_name = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")
        api_key = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
    else:
        endpoint = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "")
        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")
    return get_model_context_length(endpoint, model_name, api_key)

This helper standardizes context limit resolution across ContextRouter and IdentifyAbstractions. When explicit limits are absent, it infers configuration defaults from active provider credentials in utils.call_llm.

FetchRepo is responsible for ingesting files from either a remote GitHub repository or a local filesystem path. It normalizes paths, filters files using glob inclusion/exclusion patterns, and enforces maximum file size thresholds.

docs.title: FetchRepo.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> dict:

Description: Reads target repository paths, tokens, file patterns, and size constraints from shared. If project_name is missing, it derives a name from the URL or folder name.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state dictionary containing crawling parameters.

Returns: * dict: Parameter dictionary for exec().

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def prep(self, shared):
    repo_url = shared.get("repo_url")
    local_dir = shared.get("local_dir")
    project_name = shared.get("project_name")

    if not project_name:
        # Basic name derivation from URL or directory
        if repo_url:
            project_name = repo_url.split("/")[-1].replace(".git", "")
        else:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(local_dir))
        shared["project_name"] = project_name

    exclude_patterns = shared["exclude_patterns"]
    max_file_size = shared["max_file_size"]

    return {
        "repo_url": repo_url,
        "local_dir": local_dir,
        "token": shared.get("github_token"),
        "include_patterns": include_patterns,
        "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
        "max_file_size": max_file_size,
        "use_relative_paths": True,

Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: dict) -> list:

Description: Executes crawling using crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files based on whether repo_url is populated. Converts the returned file map into a deterministic list of (path, content) tuples.

Parameters: * prep_res (dict): Crawl configuration emitted by prep().

Returns: * list: List of (str, str) tuples representing (relative_path, file_content).

Raises: * ValueError: If no files match the inclusion/exclusion criteria.

# Implementation from nodes.py
def exec(self, prep_res):
    source = prep_res["repo_url"] or prep_res["local_dir"]
    llm_logger.info(f"NODE EXEC | node=FetchRepo | action=crawl_files | source={source}")

    if prep_res["repo_url"]:
        print(f"Crawling repository: {prep_res['repo_url']}...")
        result = crawl_github_files(
            repo_url=prep_res["repo_url"],
            token=prep_res["token"],
            include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
            exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
            max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
            use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
        )
    else:
        print(f"Crawling directory: {prep_res['local_dir']}...")

        result = crawl_local_files(
            directory=prep_res["local_dir"],
            include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
            exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
            max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
            use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"]
        )

    # Convert dict to list of tuples: [(path, content), ...]
    files_list = list(result.get("files", {}).items())
    if len(files_list) == 0:
        raise ValueError("No matching files found. Check your directory and include/exclude patterns.")

    llm_logger.info(f"NODE COMPLETE | node=FetchRepo | files_found={len(files_list)}")
    return files_list

The method routes between GitHub API crawling and local filesystem walking. It enforces validation to ensure downstream pipeline stages receive a non-empty list of source files.

docs.title: Class: ContextRouter
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Base Class: pocketflow.Node

ContextRouter analyzes total token requirements against model context limits to select an execution strategy: - "deterministic": Used when mode == "api-reference" to document every code file independently. - "direct": Used when all files fit comfortably within a single context window. - "batch": Partitions files into directory-isolated token batches for Map-Reduce processing.

docs.title: ContextRouter.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Computes total token volume for all files, calculates prompt template overhead, and determines the effective context limit with a 95% safety margin.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared state.

Returns: * tuple: Route decision ("deterministic", "direct", or "batch"), file data, effective token limits, batch sizing, token mapping, token counting function, directory tree string, and debug flags.

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def prep(self, shared):
    files_data = shared["files"]
    max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

    shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens

    # --- Token estimation setup ---
    count_tokens = create_token_counter()

    # --- Calculate prompt overhead FIRST ---
    prompt_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts")
    max_template_tokens = 0
    for subdir in ["tutorial", "advanced"]:
        template_path = os.path.join(prompt_dir, subdir, "map_abstractions.md")
        if os.path.exists(template_path):
            with open(template_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                t = count_tokens(f.read())
            max_template_tokens = max(max_template_tokens, t)

    directory_tree = self._build_directory_tree(files_data)
    tree_tokens = count_tokens(directory_tree)

    prompt_overhead = max_template_tokens + tree_tokens
    # ...
    safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
    effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
    force_batch = shared.get("force_batch", False)

    if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
        return ("deterministic", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50),
                None, None, directory_tree, False)

    if total_tokens > effective_limit or force_batch:
        return ("batch", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50),
                file_token_map, count_tokens, directory_tree, shared.get("debug", False))
    else:
        return ("direct", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50),
                None, None, directory_tree, False)

The method measures prompt template sizes and directory tree overhead before calculating the effective limit (safety_limit - prompt_overhead). If total file tokens exceed this threshold, or if --force-batch is requested, it configures Map-Reduce batching.

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> Union[str, list]:

Description: Constructs directory-coherent batches of files when the route is "batch". Files within the same directory are grouped together and chunked such that neither the token limit nor file count cap (batch_size) is exceeded.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Unpacked configuration from prep().

Returns: * str: "direct" or "deterministic" if routed directly. * list: List of batches (where each batch is a list of (index, path, content) tuples).

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def exec(self, prep_res):
    route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, count_tokens, directory_tree, debug = prep_res
    llm_logger.info(f"NODE EXEC | node=ContextRouter | action=route_decision | route={route} | files={len(files_data)} | effective_limit={effective_limit:,}")

    if route == "direct":
        return "direct"
    if route == "deterministic":
        return "deterministic"

    dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
        dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

    batches = []
    for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
        current_batch = []
        current_tokens = 0

        for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
            if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                batches.append(current_batch)
                current_batch = []
                current_tokens = 0

            current_batch.append((i, path, content))
            current_tokens += tokens

        if current_batch:
            batches.append(current_batch)

    self._directory_tree = directory_tree
    return batches

The partitioning algorithm ensures batches never mix files across different directories, maintaining structural coherence during Map operations. When a directory's files exceed the token budget or batch count, it splits the directory across multiple contiguous batches.

docs.title: ContextRouter._build_directory_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Protected (Static) Signature: def _build_directory_tree(files_data: list) -> str:

Description: Generates an indented, human-readable directory hierarchy string displaying filenames alongside their numeric indices.

Parameters: * files_data (list): List of (path, content) tuples.

Returns: * str: Indented directory tree representation.

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
@staticmethod
def _build_directory_tree(files_data):
    """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples."""
    from collections import defaultdict
    dir_files = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
        dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
        basename = os.path.basename(path)
        dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

    lines = []
    for dirname in sorted(dir_files.keys()):
        lines.append(f"{dirname}/")
        for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]):
            lines.append(f"  {fname}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

This static helper builds a concise structural overview of the repository. Including the file index (idx:{i}) in tree leaves helps the LLM link structural hierarchies with file index references in prompt contexts.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: list) -> str:

Description: Maps each valid code file index into an abstraction dictionary with a 1:1 relationship, establishes linear chapter ordering, and populates baseline relationship structures in shared.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared state. * prep_res (tuple): Prepared arguments from prep(). * exec_res (list): List of verified code indices.

Returns: * str: "default"

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
    import os
    files = shared.get("files", [])
    valid_indices = set(exec_res)
    modules = []
    chapter_order = []

    for idx, (file_path, content) in enumerate(files):
        if idx not in valid_indices:
            print(f"  - Skipping non-code file: {file_path}")
            continue

        clean_name = os.path.splitext(file_path)[0].replace(os.sep, ".").replace("/", ".")

        modules.append({
            "name": clean_name,
            "description": f"Internal API reference for `{file_path}`",
            "files": [idx],
            "original_path": file_path
        })
        chapter_order.append(len(modules) - 1)

    shared["abstractions"] = modules
    shared["chapter_order"] = chapter_order
    shared["relationships"] = {"summary": "Deterministic Internal API Reference.", "details": []}
    print(f"\033[92m[DeterministicFileMapper] Mapped {len(modules)} ACTUAL code files for exhaustive documentation.\033[0m")
    return "default"

The method skips non-code files and converts each code file's path into a dotted module name (e.g., utils/call_llm.py becomes utils.call_llm). It constructs a 1:1 abstraction entry and sets a linear chapter_order, allowing the pipeline to bypass relationship analysis nodes and move directly to WriteChapters.

Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> list:

Description: Formats the prompt template map_abstractions.md for a single file batch, executes LLM inference, parses the YAML response, and normalizes returned file indices.

Parameters: * item (dict): Individual batch item produced by prep().

Returns: * list: List of abstraction objects containing name, description, and files (as index lists).

# Implementation from nodes.py
def exec(self, item):
    batch_index = item["batch_index"]
    files = item["files"]

        project_name=item["project_name"],
        context=context,
        file_listing_for_prompt=file_listing,
        language_instruction=language_instruction,
        name_lang_hint=name_lang_hint,
        desc_lang_hint=desc_lang_hint,
        directory_tree=item.get("directory_tree", "Not available")
    )
    # ...
    response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"])
    abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)

    validated_abstractions = []
    if isinstance(abstractions, list):
        for obj in abstractions:
            if isinstance(obj, dict) and "name" in obj and "description" in obj and "file_indices" in obj:
                import re

                    if nums:
                        validated_indices.append(int(nums[0]))
                if validated_indices:
                    validated_abstractions.append({
                        "name": obj["name"],
                        "description": obj["description"],
                        "files": sorted(list(set(validated_indices)))
                    })
    return validated_abstractions

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Base Class: pocketflow.Node

IdentifyAbstractions is used when the codebase fits directly within the model's token limits without batching. It evaluates the entire codebase in a single context window to discover core abstractions.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Assembles all source files into a single context payload. If file contents exceed the safety limit (95% of maximum context), it truncates context at the boundary and prints a warning.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared state.

Returns: * tuple: Formatted context string, file listing, total file count, project name, language, cache settings, max abstraction count, thinking level, advanced mode, max tokens, and mode.

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def prep(self, shared):
    files_data = shared["files"]
    project_name = shared["project_name"]
    # ...
    def create_llm_context(files_data):
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        count_tokens = create_token_counter()

        context = ""
        file_info = []
        current_tokens = 0

        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
            entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)

            if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                print(f"\033[93mWarning: Context truncated at file index {i} ({path}) to fit within limit of {safety_limit} tokens.\033[0m")
                break

            context += entry
            file_info.append((i, path))
            current_tokens += entry_tokens

        return context, file_info

    context, file_info = create_llm_context(files_data)
    file_listing_for_prompt = "\n".join([f"- {idx} # {path}" for idx, path in file_info])
    return (context, file_listing_for_prompt, len(files_data), project_name, ...)

The nested create_llm_context helper constructs the combined file context while tracking running token counts against safety_limit. If limits are reached, it truncates gracefully to prevent out-of-context exceptions during API inference.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list:

Description: Loads identify_abstractions.md, executes inference via call_llm, parses the YAML response, and validates structural schemas including numeric range expressions (e.g. 0-4).

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Prepared configuration from prep().

Returns: * list: List of abstraction objects (name, description, files).

Raises: * ValueError: If the LLM response is not a valid list or lacks mandatory fields. * Exception: Logs errors via llm_logger and re-raises to trigger retry mechanics.

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def exec(self, prep_res):
    try:
        # ...
        prompt = prompt_template.format(
            project_name=project_name,
            context=context,
            language_instruction=language_instruction,
            max_abstraction_num=max_abstraction_num,
            name_lang_hint=name_lang_hint,
            desc_lang_hint=desc_lang_hint,
            file_listing_for_prompt=file_listing_for_prompt
        )
        # ...
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)

        # Handle index ranges like '0-3'
        for idx_entry in item["file_indices"]:
            idx_str = str(idx_entry).split("#")[0].strip()
            if '-' in idx_str:
                parts = idx_str.split('-')
                if len(parts) == 2:
                    start_idx = int(re.findall(r'\d+', parts[0])[0])
                    end_idx = int(re.findall(r'\d+', parts[1])[0])
                    for idx in range(start_idx, end_idx + 1):
                        if 0 <= idx < total_files_count:
                            validated_indices.append(idx)
                    continue
            # ...
        return validated_abstractions
    except Exception as e:
        llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
        raise e

The method includes a parsing engine for index references returned by the LLM. It handles raw integers, annotated index lines (e.g., 4 # utils/call_llm.py), and hyphenated ranges (2-5), expanding them into validated unique index arrays.

docs.title: Class: AnalyzeRelationships
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Base Class: pocketflow.Node

AnalyzeRelationships analyzes cross-module interactions and architectural dependencies between the discovered abstractions. It implements a two-pass token budget algorithm to distribute file content across abstractions without starving later entries.

docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Computes token budgets across abstractions using a two-pass allocation algorithm: - Pass 1: Allocates an equal share of the token budget to each abstraction and tracks unused headroom. - Pass 2: Redistributes unused budget from smaller abstractions to larger abstractions with remaining files.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared state.

Returns: * tuple: Context string with budget-allocated snippets, abstraction listings, abstraction count, project name, language, cache settings, thinking level, advanced mode, max tokens, and mode.

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def prep(self, shared):
    abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
    files_data = shared["files"]
    # ...
    # Two-pass allocation:
    # Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
    per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
    included_indices = set()
    abstr_results = []

    for i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
        budget = per_abstr_budget
        included_files = []
        remaining_files = []
        for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
            if idx in included_indices:
                included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                continue
            if tokens <= budget:
                included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                budget -= tokens
                included_indices.add(idx)
            else:
                remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
        abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

    # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions with remaining files
    total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
    if total_unused > 0:
        for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
            if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
                continue
            still_remaining = []
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in remaining_files:
                if idx in included_indices:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                    continue
                if tokens <= total_unused:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    total_unused -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                else:
                    still_remaining.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            abstr_results[i] = (included_files, still_remaining, 0)
    # ...

The two-pass allocator prevents context window exhaustion while maximizing code visibility. Abstractions that do not fully consume their initial budget yield remaining tokens back to the pool, allowing complex abstractions to include additional source files.

Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> dict:

Description: Formats the identify_relationships.md prompt, runs LLM inference, and validates directional relationships (from, to, label) and overall system summaries.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Prepared payload from prep().

Returns: * dict: Dictionary with "summary" (str) and "details" (list of relationship mappings).

Raises: * ValueError: If the response structure lacks expected keys or contains unparseable entries.

# Implementation from nodes.py
def exec(self, prep_res):
    try:
        # ...
        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("identify_relationships", mode=doc_mode)
        prompt = prompt_template.format(
            project_name=project_name,
            list_lang_note=list_lang_note,
            abstraction_listing=abstraction_listing,
            context=context,
            language_instruction=language_instruction,
            lang_hint=lang_hint
        )
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
        relationships_data = parse_yaml_response(response)

        validated_relationships = []
        for rel in relationships_data["relationships"]:

            to_idx = int(re.findall(r'\d+', str(rel["to_abstraction"]))[0])

                    "to": to_idx,
                    "label": rel["label"],

        return {
            "summary": relationships_data["summary"],
            "details": validated_relationships,
        }
    except Exception as e:
        llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
        raise e

Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Formats discovered abstractions and their relationships into a structural outline for topological and pedagogical ordering.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared state.

# Implementation from nodes.py
def prep(self, shared):
    abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
    relationships = shared["relationships"]
    project_name = shared["project_name"]
    language = shared.get("language", "english")

    abstraction_info_for_prompt = [f"- {i} # {a['name']}" for i, a in enumerate(abstractions)]

        # ...
        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("order_chapters", mode=doc_mode)
        prompt = prompt_template.format(
            project_name=project_name,
            list_lang_note=list_lang_note,
            abstraction_listing=abstraction_listing,
            context=context
        )
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
        ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)

        ordered_indices = []
        seen_indices = set()
        for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
            idx = int(str(entry).split("#")[0].strip())
            if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions) or idx in seen_indices:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid or duplicate index {idx}")
            ordered_indices.append(idx)
            seen_indices.add(idx)

        if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
            raise ValueError("Ordered list length does not match number of abstractions")
        return ordered_indices
    except Exception as e:
        llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
        raise e

def prep(self, shared):

    self.chapters_written_so_far = []

Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> dict:

Description: Generates the Markdown content for a single chapter. Checks the MD5 cache manifest before invoking the LLM; on cache hits, reads existing files directly. In non-API reference modes, generates a concise summary of each finished chapter to provide running context for subsequent chapters.

Parameters: * item (dict): Chapter specification dictionary from prep().

Returns: * dict: {"content": str, "hash": str, "name": str}

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def exec(self, item):
    try:
        # ...
        # Incremental Caching Logic
        if incremental and output_dir:
            hasher = hashlib.md5()
            hasher.update(file_context_str.encode("utf-8"))
            current_hash = hasher.hexdigest()
            # Check manifest and return cached content on hit
            # ...

        previous_chapters_summary = "\n---\n".join(self.chapter_summaries) if doc_mode != "api-reference" else ""

        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("draft_chapters", mode=doc_mode)
        prompt = prompt_template.format(
            language_instruction=language_instruction,
            project_name=project_name,
            abstraction_name=abstraction_name,
            chapter_num=chapter_num,
            previous_chapters_summary=previous_chapters_summary if previous_chapters_summary else "This is the first chapter.",
            file_context_str=file_context_str,
            # ...
        )
        chapter_content = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
        self.chapters_written_so_far.append(chapter_content)

        if doc_mode != "api-reference":
            summary_prompt = build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num, abstraction_name, chapter_content, language)
            chapter_summary = call_llm(summary_prompt, use_cache=True, thinking_level=None)
            self.chapter_summaries.append(f"Chapter {chapter_num} — {abstraction_name.strip()}:\n{chapter_summary}")

        return {"content": chapter_content, "hash": current_hash, "name": abstraction_name}
    except Exception as e:
        llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
        raise e

The method maintains cross-chapter coherence by passing rolling 3–5 sentence summaries instead of full chapter text, preventing context token limits from exploding across large documentation sets. It also supports incremental builds by comparing MD5 hashes of related file snippets against .doc_cache_manifest.json.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list, exec_res_list: list) -> None:

Description: Collects chapter content into shared["chapters"], writes updated .doc_cache_manifest.json metadata when incremental caching is active, and clears temporary instance tracking state.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared state. * prep_res (list): List of chapter payloads from prep(). * exec_res_list (list): List of dictionaries returned by exec().

Returns: * None

Example: 

# Implementation from nodes.py
def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
    import os, json
    shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

    # Save MD5 incremental manifest if enabled
    if shared.get("incremental"):
        output_dir = os.path.join(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared.get("project_name"))
        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")

        manifest = {}
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            try:
                with open(manifest_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    manifest = json.load(f)
            except Exception:
                pass

        for res in exec_res_list:
            if res.get("hash") and res.get("name"):
                manifest[res["name"]] = res["hash"]

        with open(manifest_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

    # Clean up temporary instance variables
    del self.chapters_written_so_far
    del self.chapter_summaries

The method extracts the generated chapter contents into shared["chapters"], persists MD5 cache entries for incremental runs, and cleans up transient summary structures.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.call_llm module serves as the primary inference dispatch interface for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It abstracts multi-provider Large Language Model (LLM) communications across Google Gemini (via the google-genai SDK with Vertex AI or standard API keys), OpenRouter, Ollama, and generic OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoints.

Key capabilities implemented in this module include: - Provider Routing & Auto-Detection: Dynamic resolution of execution providers based on environment configuration (GEMINI, OPENROUTER, OLLAMA, etc.). - Response Caching: Local disk caching mechanism backed by a JSON store (llm_cache.json) to minimize redundant inference latency and token consumption during iterative workflows. - Reasoning Effort Integration: Propagation of thinking budgets and reasoning configurations (e.g., Google GenAI ThinkingConfig, OpenRouter reasoning effort fields, and Ollama think/reasoning_effort payloads). - Context Length Resolution: Dynamic inspection and querying of endpoint context windows (e.g., OpenRouter /api/v1/models inspection, Gemini default ceilings). - Structured File-Based Logging: Isolated run logging via custom loggers to capture prompts, raw outputs, latency, and token metrics.

flowchart TD
    subgraph ClientInvocation[Client Request]
        Call[call_llm prompt, use_cache, thinking_level]
    end

    subgraph CacheLayer[Cache Verification]
        CheckCache{use_cache is True?}
        LoadCache[load_cache from llm_cache.json]
        CacheHit{Prompt in cache?}
        ReturnCached[Return cached response]
    end

    subgraph ProviderRouting[Provider Dispatch]
        GetProvider[get_llm_provider]
        GeminiCheck{Provider == 'GEMINI'?}
        CallGemini[_call_llm_gemini]
        CallGeneric[_call_llm_provider OpenRouter / Ollama]
    end

    subgraph Persistence[Response Handling]
        WriteCache[save_cache to llm_cache.json]
        ReturnResult[Return output text]
    end

    Call --> CheckCache
    CheckCache -- Yes --> LoadCache --> CacheHit
    CheckCache -- No --> GetProvider
    CacheHit -- Hit --> ReturnCached
    CacheHit -- Miss --> GetProvider
    GetProvider --> GeminiCheck
    GeminiCheck -- Yes --> CallGemini --> WriteCache
    GeminiCheck -- No --> CallGeneric --> WriteCache
    WriteCache --> ReturnResult

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial") -> str:

Description: Configures file-based logging for a pipeline invocation. It creates a dedicated log directory (controlled by the LOG_DIR environment variable or defaulting to logs), creates a sanitized filename incorporating the project name, execution mode, and a timestamp (%Y%m%d_%H%M%S), clears existing null/stale handlers from llm_logger, attaches a new logging.FileHandler, and records invocation start banners.

Parameters: * project_name (str, optional): Name of the codebase or target project. Defaults to "project". * mode (str, optional): Execution mode (e.g., "tutorial", "documentation"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The absolute or relative filesystem path to the initialized log file.

Raises: * OSError: If directory creation or file handler initialization fails due to insufficient permissions.

Example: 

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    # Sanitize project name for filesystem safety
    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
    logger.handlers.clear()
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding='utf-8')
    file_handler.setFormatter(
        logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s")
    )
    logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    logger.info(f"{'='*80}")
    logger.info(f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}")
    logger.info(f"Log file: {log_file}")
    logger.info(f"{'='*80}")

    return log_file

configure_logging() isolates system runs into discrete log files to ensure debugging output does not leak across runs. Characters outside alphanumeric and basic punctuation (-, _, .) are replaced with underscores to prevent illegal filesystem paths across operating systems. The handler operates using UTF-8 encoding and formats all outputs with timestamps, log levels, and messages.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:

Description: Fetches and caches OpenRouter's model capability catalog by performing a GET request to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models. Populates the module-level _openrouter_models_cache variable to avoid redundant network lookups on subsequent calls, returning the specific model dictionary that matches model_id.

Parameters: * model_id (str): The OpenRouter model identifier (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet").

Returns: * Optional[dict]: The model metadata payload if found; otherwise None.

Raises: * Does not raise; network and parsing errors result in an empty list cache.

Example: 

def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict:
    global _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_models_cache is None:
        try:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            _openrouter_models_cache = resp.json().get("data", [])
        except Exception:
            _openrouter_models_cache = []

    return next((m for m in _openrouter_models_cache if m.get("id") == model_id), None)

The function handles capability queries when configuring advanced parameters like extended reasoning effort. A 5-second timeout prevents indefinite blocking in degraded network conditions, and network exceptions degrade gracefully by setting _openrouter_models_cache to an empty list.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Calculates or retrieves the maximum supported token context window for a given model and API endpoint. Gemini endpoints automatically resolve to a default limit of 1,000,000 tokens. OpenRouter endpoints trigger a query against /api/v1/models to obtain the declared context_length. All other endpoints or unhandled exceptions fallback to a baseline of 100,000 tokens.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): The base or completion endpoint URL for the model provider. * model_name (str): Identifier of the target model. * api_key (str, optional): API credentials (currently unused in public endpoint query). Defaults to "".

Returns: * int: The maximum token limit for prompt and completion contexts.

Raises: * Does not raise; exceptions during HTTP queries are logged and return the default baseline.

Example: 

def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    default_limit = 100000
    try:
        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit

        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            # Safely default to 1M tokens for Gemini models
            return 1000000

        if "openrouter.ai" in endpoint_url:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            data = resp.json().get("data", [])
            for m in data:
                if m.get("id") == model_name:
                    return m.get("context_length", default_limit)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch context length for {model_name} at {endpoint_url}: {e}")

    return default_limit

This method is critical for token budgeting and file chunking mechanisms implemented across the indexing pipeline. By identifying million-token context capabilities (standard for modern Gemini architectures), the system avoids premature text truncation while preserving safety margins for smaller local models.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches a chat completion request to an OpenAI-compatible HTTP REST endpoint (e.g., OpenRouter, Ollama, vLLM). It dynamically resolves <PROVIDER>_MODEL, <PROVIDER>_BASE_URL, and <PROVIDER>_API_KEY from environment variables, prepares request headers and payloads, applies thinking/reasoning parameters if supported, posts the payload to {base_url}/v1/chat/completions, and extracts the completion text from the response structure.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The prompt string to transmit to the model. * thinking_level (Optional[str], optional): Desired reasoning level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The text generated by the model.

Raises: * ValueError: If LLM_PROVIDER, <PROVIDER>_MODEL, or <PROVIDER>_BASE_URL are missing from the environment, if the provider returns invalid JSON, or if the choices array is missing in the payload. * Exception: On HTTP errors, network timeouts, or connection failures.

Example: 

def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str = None) -> str:
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")

    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
        model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
        if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
            supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
            if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
                payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
                payload["temperature"] = 1.0
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Invalid thinking level '{thinking_level}' for model {model}. Supported efforts: {supported_efforts}")
        else:
            logger.warning(f"Model {model} does not support reasoning via OpenRouter API.")
    elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        try:
            response_json = response.json()
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            print(f"\033[93mWarning: Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}\033[0m")
            logger.warning(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}")
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}")
        response.raise_for_status()

        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            logger.warning(f"API returned 200 but no 'choices' in response: {error_detail}")
            raise ValueError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

        return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
        try:
            error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
            error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
        except:
            pass
        raise Exception(error_message)
    # ... handles ConnectionError, Timeout, RequestException, ValueError

_call_llm_provider() handles the complexities of calling generic OpenAI-compatible completion APIs. It implements specific reasoning parameters: for OpenRouter, it checks supported_efforts before modifying temperature and payload structures; for Ollama, it sets both think and reasoning_effort properties. The HTTP request enforces a connection timeout of 10 seconds and a read timeout of 300 seconds to accommodate long generation runs.
