docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str = None) -> str:

Description: Direct client implementation for Google Gemini models using the google-genai SDK. Supports authentication via Vertex AI (GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and GEMINI_LOCATION) or standalone Google AI Studio keys (GEMINI_API_KEY). Maps thinking_level values ("low", "medium", "high") to token budgets (1024, 4096, 8192) wrapped inside types.ThinkingConfig, and filters out non-text response parts (such as thought_signature) to return clean text.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The prompt string to transmit. * thinking_level (Optional[str], optional): Target thinking level for models supporting reasoning budgets. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Combined text content extracted from the candidate response parts.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment.

Example: 

def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str = None) -> str:
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        client = genai.Client(
            vertexai=True,
            project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"),
            location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1")
        )
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

    kwargs = {
        "model": model,
        "contents": [prompt]
    }

    if thinking_level:
        # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
        budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
        budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
        thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
        kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)

    response = client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)

    # Extract only text parts to avoid "non-text parts: ['thought_signature']" warnings
    if response.candidates and response.candidates[0].content.parts:
        text_parts = [part.text for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts if part.text is not None]
        return "".join(text_parts)
    return ""

This function handles Google GenAI SDK calls and reasoning configs. It maps reasoning levels into numeric token budgets via budget_map and wraps them in types.GenerateContentConfig. When parsing response parts from response.candidates[0].content.parts, it filters out non-text parts (such as reasoning metadata and thought_signature) before returning the final concatenated string.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.crawl_github_files module is responsible for ingesting source code and file trees from remote GitHub repositories. It serves as one of the underlying repository-fetching implementations called by the FetchRepo node in the computational flow.

The module provides dual retrieval mechanisms: 1. Git SSH Cloning: For SSH URLs (git@... or URLs ending with .git), the module performs a temporary shallow repository clone using git.Repo.clone_from, scans the directory tree using os.walk, applies inclusion/exclusion filters along with .gitignore patterns via pathspec, and reads file contents directly with utf-8-sig encoding. 2. GitHub REST API Traversal: For standard HTTP/HTTPS URLs, the module parses the repository owner, repository name, branch or tree commit SHA, and subdirectories. It uses the GitHub REST API (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path} and /git/trees/{tree}) to recursively traverse directories, handle rate-limit resets (403/429), parse remote .gitignore files, and fetch content via raw download URLs or base64 decoding.

Both mechanisms enforce file size limits, filter files against glob patterns, skip binary/non-text files, and output ANSI-colored terminal summaries.

docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_github_files(repo_url: str, token: str = None, max_file_size: int = 1 * 1024 * 1024, use_relative_paths: bool = False, include_patterns: Union[str, Set[str]] = None, exclude_patterns: Union[str, Set[str]] = None) -> dict:

Description: Crawls files from a specified GitHub repository URL at an optional branch, commit SHA, or subpath. Automatically selects between SSH repository cloning via GitPython and the GitHub REST API depending on the URL schema.

Under the hood: - Normalizes include_patterns and exclude_patterns into sets. - If the URL starts with git@ or ends with .git: - Creates a temporary directory using tempfile.TemporaryDirectory. - Clones the repository using git.Repo.clone_from. - Parses .gitignore using pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", ...) if present. - Recursively traverses the directory tree using os.walk, pruning excluded directories and filtering files via should_include_file. - Enforces max_file_size and reads contents using utf-8-sig. - If the URL is an HTTP/HTTPS GitHub URL: - Parses the URL components (owner, repo, optional branch/tree ref, and subdirectory path). - Fetches branches via fetch_branches or verifies trees via check_tree to resolve tree references and subdirectory paths. - Queries contents/.gitignore via the REST API to construct a pathspec matcher. - Recursively invokes fetch_contents to traverse the repository structure. - Handles API rate-limiting headers (X-RateLimit-Reset), pausing execution when limits are reached if a token is supplied. - Reads text contents via download_url HTTP requests or decodes base64 content payloads. - Prints a color-coded summary to standard output and returns a dictionary containing the path-to-content map and execution statistics.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): Target GitHub repository URL (e.g., 'https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/main/subdir' or 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git'). * token (str | None, optional): GitHub personal access token for authenticating private repositories and raising API rate limits. Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum file size in bytes to read into memory. Defaults to 1048576 (1 MB). * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): If True, returns dictionary keys relative to the specified URL subdirectory rather than repository root. Defaults to False. * include_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): File pattern or set of glob patterns to include (e.g., {"*.py", "*.md"}). If None, all files are included. * exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): File pattern or set of glob patterns to exclude (e.g., {"test/*", "*.png"}). If None, no patterns are excluded.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary structured as: - "files" (dict[str, str]): Mapping of relative file paths to string file contents. - "stats" (dict[str, Any]): Metadata dictionary containing downloaded_count, skipped_count, skipped_files, base_path, include_patterns, exclude_patterns, and optionally source or error.

Raises: * ValueError: If repo_url cannot be parsed into valid GitHub repository components (owner and repository name). * Exception: If GitHub API rate limits are exceeded without a token provided, or if git clone operations fail.

Example: 

from utils.crawl_github_files import crawl_github_files

result = crawl_github_files(
    repo_url="https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/main/pydantic",
    token="ghp_exampletoken12345",
    max_file_size=512 * 1024,
    use_relative_paths=True,
    include_patterns={"*.py"},
    exclude_patterns={"tests/*"}
)

files = result["files"]
print(f"Downloaded {len(files)} files.")

docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Internal recursive helper within crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_contents(path: str) -> None:

Description: Recursively navigates the GitHub repository hierarchy using the REST API GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}: - Appends the query parameter ref if a branch/commit is specified. - If rate-limited (403/429), reads X-RateLimit-Reset, sleeps until the quota resets, and retries the request. - Iterates over items returned in the directory listing: - Directories (dir): Checks gitignore_spec and exclude_patterns. If excluded, prints an ANSI exclusion log; otherwise, recursively calls fetch_contents(item["path"]). - Files (file): Checks patterns via should_include_file and enforces max_file_size. Downloads content using download_url or falls back to decoding base64 payloads from item["url"]. Updates the outer files dictionary and tracking counters.

Parameters: * path (str): Repository directory path to inspect.

Returns: * None (Updates the enclosing files dictionary and counter state in-place).

Raises: * Exception: If GitHub API rate limits are hit without a configured token.

Example: 

# Internal invocation within crawl_github_files

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.crawl_local_files module provides local filesystem directory crawling and source ingestion capabilities for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. It is utilized by the FetchRepo node when local directory paths (--dir) are targeted instead of remote Git repositories.

The module mirrors the functional interface and filtering logic of utils.crawl_github_files, enabling uniform downstream processing. It features: - Recursive directory traversal via os.walk with in-place directory pruning to avoid traversing excluded directory branches. - Automatic .gitignore pattern loading and matching using pathspec.PathSpec with gitwildmatch rules. - Glob-based include and exclude pattern filtering using fnmatch. - File size threshold validation to avoid loading large assets into memory. - Safe text decoding with utf-8-sig encoding, filtering out binary and non-text files. - Formatted ANSI terminal summary reporting with detailed metrics on processed, excluded, oversized, and unreadable files.

docs.title: crawl_local_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_local_files(directory: str, include_patterns: set[str] | None = None, exclude_patterns: set[str] | None = None, max_file_size: int | None = None, use_relative_paths: bool = True) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:

Description: Performs a single-pass traversal of a local directory, applying hierarchical directory pruning, .gitignore rules, inclusion/exclusion wildcard filters, file size limits, and UTF-8 encoding checks.

Under the hood, the function performs the following steps: 1. Validation: Checks if directory exists using os.path.isdir(), raising ValueError if the directory is missing. 2. Gitignore Discovery: Checks for a .gitignore file located directly under directory. If found, parses its lines using pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", ...) with utf-8-sig encoding. If parsing fails, logs a warning and continues without .gitignore filtering. 3. Recursive Traversal & Directory Pruning: - Walks the directory tree using os.walk(directory). - Iterates through subdirectories (dirs), calculating their relative path to directory. - Checks subdirectories against gitignore_spec and exclude_patterns (normalizing trailing /* wildcards). - Dynamically mutates dirs in-place by removing excluded directories, preventing unnecessary recursive traversal into ignored subtrees (such as node_modules, .git, or build caches). - Sorts the remaining dirs in-place for deterministic alphabetical traversal ordering. 4. File Filtering and Ingestion: - Iterates over sorted files within the current directory. - Computes relative paths if use_relative_paths=True, or absolute/verbatim paths otherwise. - Tests relpath against gitignore_spec.match_file(relpath). Skips and logs with ANSI gray if matched. - Tests relpath against exclude_patterns using fnmatch.fnmatch. Skips and logs if matched. - Tests relpath against include_patterns using fnmatch.fnmatch (if include_patterns is provided). Skips if no pattern matches. - Inspects file size via os.path.getsize(filepath). Skips and logs with ANSI red if max_file_size is exceeded. - Reads text contents using open(filepath, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig"). - Catches UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError for binary/non-text files and records them in skipped_non_text. - Successfully read files are added to files_dict[relpath]. 5. Summary Reporting: - Prints a formatted terminal summary to standard output detailing total discovered items, processed count, excluded count, oversized files, and unparseable non-text files. 6. Return: Returns a dictionary mapping the "files" key to the populated path-to-content dictionary.

Parameters: * directory (str): Target root filesystem path to crawl. * include_patterns (set[str] | None, optional): Set of wildcard glob patterns to include (e.g., {"*.py", "*.js"}). If None or empty, all non-excluded files are considered. Defaults to None. * exclude_patterns (set[str] | None, optional): Set of wildcard glob patterns to ignore (e.g., {"tests/*", "*.log"}). Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int | None, optional): Maximum allowable file size in bytes. Files exceeding this threshold are skipped. Defaults to None. * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): Flag indicating whether the dictionary keys should be relative to directory (True) or use full filepath strings (False). Defaults to True.

Returns: * dict[str, dict[str, str]]: A dictionary containing: - "files" (dict[str, str]): Mapping of relative (or full) file path strings to their decoded file text contents.

Raises: * ValueError: If directory does not exist or is not a valid directory.

Example: 

from utils.crawl_local_files import crawl_local_files

# Crawl a local project folder ignoring caches and tests
result = crawl_local_files(
    directory="./my_project",
    include_patterns={"*.py", "*.md"},
    exclude_patterns={"tests/*", "__pycache__/*", "*.pyc"},
    max_file_size=512 * 1024,
    use_relative_paths=True
)

files = result["files"]
for path, content in files.items():
    print(f"Loaded {path} ({len(content)} characters)")

File: utils/prompts.py

The utils.prompts module provides programmatic, inline prompt constructors and configuration generators for internal pipeline nodes within Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. Unlike the dynamic file-based prompt templates loaded from the prompts/{mode}/ directory, the builders in this module generate standardized, deterministic prompt strings and static configuration files required by core nodes during file filtering, chapter summarization, and documentation site generation.

docs.title: Architectural Role and Workflow
docs.text:
The functions in utils.prompts are utilized across different stages of the documentation pipeline:

  1. File Filtering Stage: build_code_file_filter_prompt formats file manifests into structured prompts so that LLM evaluation nodes (e.g., DeterministicFileMapper) can isolate true code modules from configuration, markup, assets, and project scaffolding.
  2. Iterative Summarization Stage: build_chapter_summary_prompt generates four-dimensional technical brief extraction prompts after a chapter is written, producing context injected into subsequent chapter generation passes.
  3. Artifact Generation Stage: build_mkdocs_config transforms hierarchical navigation snippets into a production-ready mkdocs.yml configuration targeting the Material for MkDocs theme.

    end

        BCSP --> LLMSummarizer[LLM Summarization Call]
        LLMSummarizer --> TechBrief[Structured Technical Brief]
        TechBrief --> NextChapter[Subsequent Chapter Context]
    end

docs.title: build_code_file_filter_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:

Description: Constructs the system/user instruction prompt passed to language models in api-reference mode to distinguish executable source code modules from non-code project files. The prompt presents the complete codebase file index alongside explicit exclusion rules (filtering out UI layouts, XML/JSON configs, static assets, and build manifests) and commands the model to return strictly a YAML list of numerical file indices.

Parameters: * project_name (str): The name or identifier of the target codebase. * file_listing (str): A pre-formatted, numbered or indexed manifest of all files discovered in the target repository.

Returns: * str: A formatted prompt ready for direct submission to an LLM completion API.

Raises: * This function does not explicitly raise exceptions; standard string formatting operations apply.

Example: 

def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:
    """Build the prompt for DeterministicFileMapper to filter non-code files.

    Used in api-reference mode to identify which files are actual code modules
    (APIs, functions, classes, business logic) vs. UI layouts, configs, assets.
    """
    return (
        f"For the project `{project_name}`, here is the list of all files in the codebase:\n\n"
        f"{file_listing}\n\n"
        f"Your task is to identify WHICH of these files are ACTUAL CODE files that contain "
        f"APIs, functions, classes, or core business logic.\n"
        f"EXCLUDE: UI layouts (like .xaml, .storyboard, .html), configuration files "
        f"(like .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini), static assets, build scripts "
        f"(like .csproj, .sln), and documentation.\n\n"
        f"Return ONLY a YAML list of the file indices that should be documented as code modules.\n\n"
        f"```yaml\n- 0\n- 1\n- 3\n```"
    )

The function relies on rigid prompt constraints to prevent output hallucinations. By providing a strict YAML template (yaml\n- 0\n- 1\n- 3\n) in the instruction, it enforces machine-parseable outputs that can be deserialized directly into integer indices by calling nodes such as DeterministicFileMapper. It specifically targets common non-code extensions across ecosystems (e.g., .xaml, .storyboard, .html, .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini, .csproj, .sln), ensuring downstream token budgets are not expended on non-executable files.

docs.title: build_chapter_summary_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:

Description: Constructs an analytical prompt that instructs the LLM to summarize a newly generated documentation chapter into a structured technical brief across four specific architectural dimensions. This brief is subsequently retained in the execution state to maintain inter-chapter context and prevent semantic drift across subsequent chapters.

Parameters: * chapter_num (int): The numerical index or order of the current chapter. * abstraction_name (str): The title, architectural domain, or abstraction layer represented in the chapter. * chapter_content (str): The full Markdown or text body of the generated chapter. * language (str, optional): The target natural language for the output summary. Defaults to "english".

Returns: * str: The complete prompt instructing the model to generate a four-part structured technical brief.

Raises: * This function does not explicitly raise exceptions.

Example: 

def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str,
                                  chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:
    """Build the prompt for generating a technical summary of a written chapter."""
    lang_instruction = (
        f"Write the entire summary in {language.capitalize()}. "
        if language.lower() != "english" else ""
    )
    return (
        f"{lang_instruction}"
        f"Summarize the following documentation chapter as a structured technical brief. "
        f"For EACH of the 4 points below, write 3-5 concise technical sentences:\n\n"
        f"(1) **Component Scope & Responsibility**: What is the main technical domain this "
        f"chapter covers? What problems does it solve and what role does it play in the system?\n\n"
        f"(2) **Key Technical Elements**: What are the specific classes, services, functions, "
        f"data models, or protocols discussed? Name them and describe their concrete roles.\n\n"
        f"(3) **Implementation Patterns & Architecture**: What design patterns, communication "
        f"protocols, data flow strategies, error handling mechanisms, or security measures "
        f"are covered? How are they implemented?\n\n"
        f"(4) **System Integration & Dependencies**: How does this component interface with "
        f"other parts of the system? What does it consume from or provide to other components? "
        f"What are the key integration points?\n\n"
        f"---\n"
        f"Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}\n"
        f"{chapter_content}"
    )

The prompt construction enforces a strict technical taxonomy by segmenting the analysis into: (1) Component Scope & Responsibility, (2) Key Technical Elements, (3) Implementation Patterns & Architecture, and (4) System Integration & Dependencies. When localized documentation generation is requested (i.e., language is not "english"), the function dynamically prepends a localization directive (Write the entire summary in {language.capitalize()}.). The structured output guarantees that key architectural invariants, interface definitions, and dependency contracts remain accessible to subsequent pipeline nodes without exceeding token context limits.

docs.title: build_mkdocs_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str) -> str:

Description: Generates the text content for a standard mkdocs.yml configuration file supporting Material for MkDocs. It configures code block copy buttons, PyMdown Extensions syntax highlighting with line numbering anchors, inline code highlighting, and Mermaid diagram rendering via custom super-fences.

Parameters: * site_name (str): The title of the documentation website displayed in the navigation header. * nav_yaml (str): A YAML-formatted string representing the navigation hierarchy generated by the pipeline.

Returns: * str: The complete YAML configuration string ready to be written to mkdocs.yml.

Raises: * This function does not explicitly raise exceptions.

Example: 

def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str) -> str:
    """Build a complete mkdocs.yml for local --mkdocs output."""
    # Extract nav items from nav_snippet (strip the "nav:" header line)
    nav_lines = nav_yaml.split("\n")
    nav_body = "\n".join(nav_lines[1:]) if nav_lines else ""

    return (
        f"site_name: '{site_name}'\n"
        f"theme:\n"
        f"  name: material\n"
        f"  features:\n"
        f"    - content.code.copy\n"
        f"markdown_extensions:\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.highlight:\n"
        f"      anchor_linenums: true\n"
        f"      use_pygments: true\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.superfences:\n"
        f"      custom_fences:\n"
        f"        - name: mermaid\n"
        f"          class: mermaid\n"
        f"          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.inlinehilite\n"
        f"nav:\n"
        f"  - Home: index.md\n"
        f"{nav_body}\n"
    )

The function extracts individual navigation entries by splitting nav_yaml across newline boundaries and stripping the initial nav: declaration line via \n.join(nav_lines[1:]). It then embeds the resulting indented navigation tree beneath a hardcoded - Home: index.md root item. The configuration registers the pymdownx.superfences custom fence using the Python class resolver !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format, enabling client-side rendering of embedded Mermaid diagrams.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.token_utils module provides token calculation, estimation, and logging utilities across the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. Because Large Language Model (LLM) context windows are constrained by strict input token thresholds, node executions must monitor prompt sizes and log token consumption metrics before dispatching payloads to downstream LLM APIs.

This module encapsulates: 1. Lazy Singleton Encoding Initialization: Dynamically loads and caches the cl100k_base BPE (Byte-Pair Encoding) model from tiktoken upon first invocation. 2. Graceful Token Counting & Heuristic Fallbacks: Accurately counts tokens via tiktoken.encode() and falls back to a character-ratio heuristic (len(text) // 4) if tiktoken is unavailable or encounters initialization failures. 3. Structured Token Analytics Logging: Computes prompt capacity utilization percentages and breakdown metrics per node execution, emitting formatted ANSI-colored diagnostics to stdout and structured log entries to the shared llm_logger.

docs.title: _get_encoding()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_encoding() -> Optional[tiktoken.Encoding]:

Description: Retrieves or lazily instantiates the module-level singleton _encoding instance. It attempts to load the standard OpenAI cl100k_base tokenizer schema via tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base"). If tiktoken raises any exception (e.g., missing network access for first-time vocabulary downloads, unsupported platform dependencies, or corrupt vocabulary cache files), the exception is swallowed and _encoding remains None. This design ensures that token counting never crashes the pipeline.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * Optional[tiktoken.Encoding]: The initialized tiktoken encoding instance, or None if initialization failed.

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated; all internal Exception instances during retrieval are caught and handled.

Example: 

def _get_encoding():
    global _encoding
    if _encoding is None:
        try:
            _encoding = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        except Exception:
            _encoding = None
    return _encoding

_get_encoding manages the global tokenizer cache lifecycle through lazy instantiation. By isolating the tiktoken.get_encoding call inside a guarded try/except block, the function provides an operational guarantee that network or runtime issues within the tokenizer library do not halt execution. Subsequent calls re-use the resolved _encoding reference without re-executing tokenizer parsing routines.

docs.title: count_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def count_tokens(text: str) -> int:

Description: Calculates the total number of BPE tokens in a provided text string. If the input text is empty or falsy, it immediately returns 0. When the cl100k_base tokenizer is available via _get_encoding(), the function returns the exact token length from len(enc.encode(text)). If the tokenizer is unavailable (for example, if initialization failed), it falls back to the deterministic character approximation formula len(text) // 4, standard for English and code-heavy LLM contexts.

Parameters: * text (str): The raw text or prompt content whose tokens need to be calculated.

Returns: * int: Total token count (either exact BPE token length or heuristic estimate).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def count_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Count tokens using tiktoken, with fallback to chars/4."""
    if not text:
        return 0
    enc = _get_encoding()
    if enc:
        return len(enc.encode(text))
    return len(text) // 4

The function handles edge cases where text is passed as an empty string, None, or whitespace by returning 0 immediately. When processing source code or structured node prompts, enc.encode(text) accurately accounts for indentation tokens, special syntax symbols, and vocabulary splits. The fallback len(text) // 4 ensures downstream nodes can still monitor rough capacity limits in restricted environments where external dependencies fail.

docs.title: log_token_estimation()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def log_token_estimation(node_name: str, prompt_content: str, max_tokens: int, token_usage: dict = None) -> None:

Description: Performs token usage analysis for an execution step and emits formatted diagnostics to both stdout and logger. It calculates the prompt token count using count_tokens(prompt_content) and derives the percentage of context capacity utilized (token_count / max_tokens * 100). If an optional token_usage breakdown dictionary is supplied, it calculates relative percentages for each sub-component (e.g., file contents, system instructions, metadata).

The formatted output is emitted to the console using ANSI yellow escape codes (\033[93m...\033[0m) for visibility during interactive runs, and simultaneously written to the "llm_logger" handler via logger.info().

Parameters: * node_name (str): Identifier of the executing workflow node (e.g., "node_file_summary"). * prompt_content (str): Complete text payload intended for the model prompt. * max_tokens (int): Upper bound limit of tokens allowed for the target model or node context. * token_usage (dict, optional): Mapping of descriptive labels to individual token count integers representing prompt components. Defaults to None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def log_token_estimation(node_name: str, prompt_content: str, max_tokens: int,
                         token_usage: dict = None) -> None:
    token_count = count_tokens(prompt_content)
    percentage = (token_count / max_tokens) * 100 if max_tokens else 0

    # Build token usage string if provided
    usage_str = ""
    if token_usage:
        parts = []
        for label, value in token_usage.items():
            pct = (value / token_count * 100) if token_count else 0
            parts.append(f"{label}={value:,} ({pct:.0f}%)")
        usage_str = " | " + " | ".join(parts)

    # Console output (yellow) with token usage
    print(f"\033[93m[Token Analytics] {node_name}: {token_count:,} / {max_tokens:,} tokens ({percentage:.1f}% capacity){usage_str}\033[0m")

    # File log with node context and token usage
    logger.info(f"NODE EXEC | node={node_name} | prompt_tokens={token_count:,} / {max_tokens:,} ({percentage:.1f}% capacity){usage_str}")

log_token_estimation provides real-time monitoring of token budget consumption before LLM API invocation. It safely guards against division-by-zero errors when max_tokens or token_count are zero. The optional token_usage parameter allows nodes to pass sub-breakdowns (such as individual source files or dependency context), which are formatted into percentage-of-total strings and appended to both the terminal output and structured file log records.
